description:
What `jobs` lists in command and process substitutions and in pipeline stages: the jobs' states
when they started, as bash lists them there, so a throttle that counts running jobs ends.

Each case name starts with `job listings: `.

cases.name: job listings: a finished job is not running in a substitution or a stage
cases.script: sleep 0.2 & sleep 1; echo "r=[$(jobs -r)]"; jobs -r | wc -l; n=$(jobs -rp | wc -l); echo n=$n

cases.name: job listings: a throttle on jobs -r
cases.script:
for i in $(seq 10); do
  while [ "$(jobs -r | wc -l)" -ge 4 ]; do sleep 0.1; done
  sleep 0.3 &
done
wait; echo done

cases.name: job listings: a throttle on jobs -p
cases.script:
for i in $(seq 10); do
  while [ "$(jobs -p | wc -l)" -ge 4 ]; do sleep 0.1; done
  sleep 0.3 &
done
wait; echo done

cases.name: job listings: a substitution lists the running jobs and the last one started
cases.script:
sleep 0.1 & sleep 0.1 & sleep 1
echo "c=[$(jobs)]"; echo "p=[$(jobs -p | wc -l)]"; x=$(jobs | cat); echo "x=[$x]"
f() { jobs; }; x=$(f); echo "f=[$x]"; cat <(jobs); jobs | cat; echo top; jobs; wait
sleep 3 & sleep 0.1 & sleep 3 & sleep 0.1 & sleep 1
echo "c=[$(jobs)]"; echo "p=[$(jobs -p | wc -l)] r=[$(jobs -r | wc -l)]"; kill %1 %3; wait

cases.name: job listings: only a jobs stage lists the jobs of its shell
